title: Develop a business plan for a small business

lessons.title: Purpose and structure of a business plan
lessons.html:
Why you need a business plan

A business plan is a written document that describes what the business will do, how it will do it, and how it will make money. It has three main uses:

  • Planning: it forces you to think through every part of the business before you spend money.
  • Funding: banks, the Land Bank, development finance institutions and investors usually ask for a business plan before they lend or invest.
  • Managing: it gives targets against which you measure progress.

The main sections

  1. Executive summary: one page that explains the business, the opportunity, the money needed and the expected results. Write it last.
  2. Business description: name, legal form (for example sole proprietor, partnership, private company or co-operative), location, owners and vision.
  3. Products and services: what you sell and why customers will buy it.
  4. Market analysis: who your customers are, how big the market is, who your competitors are and what prices they charge.
  5. Marketing plan: how you will reach customers: product, price, place (distribution) and promotion.
  6. Operations plan: land, buildings, equipment, suppliers, production process and quality control.
  7. Management and staff: who will run the business, their skills, and staff needed.
  8. Financial plan: start-up costs, projected income statement, cash flow forecast and break-even.
  9. Risks: what could go wrong and how you will manage it.

Example

Thandi wants to start a small packing and cold storage service for emerging citrus growers near her village. Her business plan describes the cold room she needs, the growers who have agreed to use it, the fee per bin, the cost of electricity and a generator, and the loan she needs. It also lists risks such as load-shedding and a poor season, with plans to manage them.

lessons.title: Market, operations and financial planning
lessons.html:
Researching the market

Good market research makes the plan believable. Gather facts by:

  • talking to possible customers and asking what they buy, how much and at what price;
  • visiting competitors and noting their prices and service;
  • checking prices at the fresh produce market or with buyers;
  • using information from industry associations and the Department of Agriculture.

Write down a clear description of your target customer and why they will choose you, for example better quality, lower price, closer location or a reliable service.

Operations

Describe step by step how the product is produced and delivered. List equipment with prices, suppliers, licences and permits needed, and the number of workers with their wages. Do not forget legal requirements such as business registration, tax registration with SARS, UIF and compliance with labour and safety laws.

Financial planning

  • Start-up costs: equipment, building work, first stock, deposits, registration.
  • Projected income statement: expected sales minus costs for each year, showing profit or loss.
  • Cash flow forecast: money in and money out month by month. Farming income is seasonal, so the forecast shows when you will need extra cash.
  • Break-even: the sales level where income covers all costs. Break-even quantity = fixed costs divided by (selling price per unit minus variable cost per unit).

Example: Thandi's fixed costs are R120 000 per year. She charges R50 per bin and her variable cost is R20 per bin. Break-even is R120 000 divided by R30, which is 4 000 bins a year.

Presenting and using the plan

Keep the plan clear, honest and supported by evidence. Attach quotes, letters of intent from customers and CVs. Review the plan at least once a year and update it when circumstances change.

Key points

  • A business plan helps you plan, raise funds and manage.
  • Write the executive summary last.
  • Base the market analysis on real research with customers and competitors.
  • Include start-up costs, income statement, cash flow and break-even.
  • Review and update the plan regularly.
